question_text: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a sore throat, nonproductive cough, and bloody urine for 3 days. He has had 2 similar episodes involving a sore throat and bloody urine over the past year. His sister has systemic lupus erythematosus. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). Serum studies show a urea nitrogen concentration of 8 mg/dL and a creatinine concentration of 1.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows acanthocytes and red blood cell casts. Renal ultrasonography shows no abnormalities. A renal biopsy is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Question
                    A 17-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a sore throat, nonproductive cough, and bloody urine for 3 days. He has had 2 similar episodes involving a sore throat and bloody urine over the past year. His sister has systemic lupus erythematosus. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). Serum studies show a urea nitrogen concentration of 8 mg/dL and a creatinine concentration of 1.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows acanthocytes and red blood cell casts. Renal ultrasonography shows no abnormalities. A renal biopsy is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. IgA mesangial deposition
opb. Capillary wire looping
opc. Splitting of the glomerular basement membrane
opd. Granular deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3 complement
ope. Effacement of the foot processes

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation with sore throat, bloody urine, and glomerular involvement suggests a glomerulonephritis. Given the normal renal function and family history of autoimmune disease, a renal biopsy is indicated to identify specific glomerular changes. The most likely finding on renal biopsy in this case would be granular deposits of IgG, IgM, and C3 complement, consistent with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis type I.
